personal.about:
I am a Christian. However, I believe in supporting the Jews/Judaism because I'm a strong believer that without Judaism there would be no Christianity. I therefore wear not only the Christian Cross but also the Star of David and could care less what kind of reactions I get from people whom do not support the Jews. As a Christian I have to acknowledge the old testament as we know it comes from the Jewish Torah and Tanakh. So I also believe any Christian that opposes the original chosen ones of God aren't really the Christians I care to associate myself with.
I am a 57 year old man in Clarksville, Tn., U.S.A.. Drove trucks and did security on the side for the better part of 36 years. Am now retired because of having been stricken with stage 4 cancer in Nov. 2016 and had a heart attack since. Also have emphysema and COPD. Although you'd never know it by looking at me now. LOL! 
I was never suppose to survive according to all the doctors. But, we have a very powerful and merciful God in the God of Abraham and I am now in remission. Although I am as I like to call reluctantly retired, there is not a day goes by I don't give thanks to God for not taking me from my Grandchildren because they have at a young age lost enough for now so to speak. 
I spend my days with the Grandchildren, keeping in touch with family and friends and passing Gods word onto others. 
Shalom to all!

personal.about:
PLEASE READ. Mostly here to find my Bashert. MY CURRENT LOCATION IS SOUTH AFRICA where I work. I am American. I will likely return to NY or make Aliyah when my contract ends. Hard working, nice, down to earth Jewish Girl who loves to have adventures and to share a home cooked meal. I have lived and explored the US and keep in touch with friends and family in all four corners. At the end of a Shomer Shabbat I enjoy heading to a dive bar for live Music. I LOVE art of every form. I wear dresses and skirts 99% of the time, even in the winter. I have been told I am an anomaly with an unusual amount of Bitachon who can pitch a tent, build a campfire, understand Ayn Rand, the Tanya and Harry Potter. I am truly just a Jew on a Journey, a Spiritual being having a very Human Experience. My location is currently South Africa where I work as an international development volunteer. My connectivity is limited but I trust Hashem in all things. If you are interested please be in touch in a way that I can respond to. Despite my work in rural South Africa I have a strong connection to the Rabbis at Sandton Chabad and Yardley Shul in Bucks County PA. 

Having someone to share my love of tikkun olam work is important but he does not need to be by my side as I do it, although that could be fun. Long term I am looking to create a Jewish Home that my future grandchildren will want to visit for love of life and as a Jewish person. I am quite happy in the secular world escaping each week in to Shabbat for time to rest and connect. More often than not I am most comfortable in a Chabad Shul. I didn't grow up observant. I have been keeping a kosher (not PAS) at home for 5 years, yes even in the Bush of South Africa. My children are grown, 2 are married, one in the American Military. I listen to secular music, eat out, enjoy movies, concerts, backpacking, the beach. My daughter is making Alyah and I would not mind following her one day. Life is full of uncertainties, I would like a partner to face those with.



About him
A guy who understands that life is about balance, everything in moderation is ideal for me. Someone who feels like home, on a mountain top, the beach, the city, or stuck on the side of the road. I am looking for a partner to grow and explore all life has to offer. My bashert must have patience with wanderlust. An understanding that life’s journey is never easy, finding someone to share it with makes it easier. And thus more worth it. I am willing to do the work. My work will sometimes limit communication to email or Whatsap.
 
I am looking for a partner. A Zayde for my future grandchildren. A man who can lead a sader, sing eshet chayil, support my desires for international development work and is open to adventures from time to time. I want to learn and teach from all those I encounter, especially my husband. A Noah, he does not have to be perfect, only perfect for me. I love and respect the role of men and believe that both men and women have important roles to play in the world. I want to be the reason a man feels safe in the world, to be his soft place to land.

I currently hold the office of Original Jurisdiction Govenor of Oklahoma State and Territories. 

I own a 25 acer ranch/farm in Eastern Oklahoma and raise chickens for eggs... Once a week I pack the eggs up and donate them to a local food bank in Okay, Oklahoma sponsored by their local churches "Manna House". The past 4 years I have donated approximatly 400 dozon clean free range eggs and 180 hours community service packing food boxes for the needy in this community.

Up until last year I housed over 100 Laying hens, unforchunetly the ranch what hit by a freak storm from the NE and a tornato out of the NW and losses were high. Since then my flock has dwindled down to 19 laying hens. In October I purchased 14 Americans "Easter Eggers"  to begin increasing my flock, they should begin laying this spring.

As someone who is on a journey to become more observant, it was a pleasure spending Shabbos with Ellen and Dov. Everyone I met there was very friendly. I look forward to spending more time with them. I highly recommend anyone in in the Hollywood Beach area to reach out to Ellen and Dov.

Our family was so fortunate to meet such a special couple who are changing Klal Yisroel in southern Florida. Their warmth and graciousness know no bounds. They infuse a Shabbat atomsphere that makes every guest so welcome. We enjoyed spending Shabbat with you in an  incredible and delightful atomsphere which truly enhanced our trip. Thank you so much Dov and Ellen for all you do, and may you be blessed with all good things in life
Had an amazing Shabbos with Rabbi Dov and his Rebetzin Ellen food was amazing, accommodations where perfect and all the guests where great!!!!! Thanks so much!

This past Shabbos I closed a chapter in the book of my life and I am so happy that the Tilles' were a part of it. They have more than a meal in their beachfront home - they have a community! 

To say that they have chesed and ahavas Yisrael is just not enough to describe the warmth that this family exuberates. I have enjoyed all my Shabbosem in the last few months and I will miss Dov and Elk dearly. Their meals are filled with singing, lots of delicious food and very interesting guests from all over the world. 

I am certainly hoping we either meet again at Daven with Dov or in Jerusalem soon! 

Thank you again and looking forward to only coming together for simchas!

What an incredible shabbos! As soon as I walked into the Tilles home I felt the warmth and total chesed that fills their rooms. Dov was an incredible host! His wife was not present so he had multiple roles to fill and he did so elegently. Everyone mentioned that this was "nothing" and I needed to come back when Mrs. Tilles was there. Honestly, I cannot imagine what could have been better! I had a few great conversations with Mr. Tilles and I loved my shabbos there. The minyan was great, as were the variety of guests who shared shabbos with us. Incredible hospitality, and warm people, is how I can sum up my stay in a few words. Thanks again and really look forward to another shabbos with you!

Dov and Ellen thank you so much for having me. It was great to get to know you both. The food, company and view of the beach was great. And a public service announcement to any non vegetarians reading this: don't be scared off! The food is better than Almost any meat meal. And with getting to meet many locals and tourists alike It's a great place to spend a Shabbat.

The food, the chessed, the warmth, the people, there is no end to wonderful shabbos I experienced at what comes quite close to Avraham's tent. The rabbi and the rebbetzin are fun, great to talk to, and the shabbos seudot and davening completes the puzzle for the amazing weekend :)
Dov and Ellen are great hosts and it's always a pleasure to enjoy such meaningful and holy Shabbasos at their home.
Always a treat to spend Shabbat with hosts of such superb charachter and yiras Shamayim as Dov and Ellen.
You definitly don't want to miss out on such an amazing Shabbat experience. The atmosphere is relaxing, enjoyable, friendly, and very tasty!
The experience being  a guest by such a wonderful family is priceless.
Incredible hosts!  Ellen is a great cook and there Shabbos table is always warm and friendly. Great people who always make it a great shabbos experience.

If you have a chance to be by the Tilles's don't miss it! They are amazing.  Dov & Ellen both have true hearts of gold.  We've been by them so many times... and will be, please G-d, many times more.  I cannot even begin to describe how amazing is the experience of staying there.  Tons of incredible shabbos food cooked fresh by Ellen every week, d'var Torahs, brachot, and soulful davening.  Kol hakavod to you both!!!!!!
Baruch Hashem i had an unforgettable time by the tille's family. They are very nice hosts, with a real sense of Hachnassas Orchim. Thanks to Mrs. Tilles, the food was delicious!

personal.about:
Welcome to our home. We are so excited to have you. We are a family of 3+1.....we count our 4-legged child in the numbers, but he doesn't join us for dinner!
We are working to become a Shomer Shabbos family, B"H, and it's something we are taking one step at a time. We keep Kosher-style, meaning that we don't mix, but we do not yet have two sets of everything. We're working on remedying that, but for now, we use disposables for Shabbos, especially when we have company. (Fewer dishes to wash!)
Meals tend to be traditional - chicken soup, roast chicken, green salad, veggies, etc, and there is always chocolate somewhere in the dessert, as well as a non-chocolate choice!
I am an American Sign Language interpreter, so I ALWAYS welcome Deaf and Hard of Hearing guests. We hope to see you soon!!

Hi there, its great to finally get a hold of you I've been trying to reach you for months. Well now that I've got you, i would like to tell you, that i would really love if you would grace us with your presence for a shabbat meal. My wife makes the best food, and in my opinion "company is never too much and always too little". Yes i know what your thinking,  'how can we enjoy ourselves when my son is jumping around on the couch and going on every bodies nerves' well i got news for you :that's just the beginning, Once he goes to sleep there is usually at least three hours up for discussing anything from music, movies, philosophy, religion, culture, stories of the past, politics, or we can just talk on what to add to this list. Well all kidding aside i would really love to have you over for shabbat and can't wait to hear from you.

-yours truly

endorsements.body:
Be A Guest of Amy and Avrohom Klein if you like or love sharing a traditional Shabbat with a warm loving, learned, open minded Hamishe family that includes some of the best behaved children on the planet. The previous compliments apply equally to Rabbi and Rebbetzin Fink family who were also guests of the Kleins.
Skip this Shabbos celebration if :
1-You don't like delicious food.
2- You can't appreciate L'chaim with 17 year old single malt scotcth.
3- You cannot appreciate a well thought out relevant Devar Torah.
4- You don't appreciate a  discussion with learned men and women who are giving respectful  consideration to your far less learned opinion.
5- You don't want to be with people genuinely interested in becoming better acquainted with you.
6- You don't want to bear witness to a father performing the mitzvoth  " Teach Your Children Well" then don't watch Avrohom telling his children the story of the "Hidden Tsadik" as they listen attentively.
The Klein Family home has become my fa
Was really nice meeting you, looking forward to the next time.

My wife and I had a wonderful time at the Kleins. We were treated with open arms by the parents and well behaved children as well. The food was delicious and the accommodations were cozy. We had a pleasant experience and we hope to join them again in the future.
Thank you for your hospitality!  I enjoyed your company!

Avrohom and Amy Klein were great hosts they make me feel like home and the food was delicious 
very nice people and very nice family especially there kids where very well behaved!!!!!
One of my FAVORITE places to go for Shabbos!  Looking forward to seeing you guys this week...

A wonderful and warm family. I had the pleasure of shabbat lunch at their home and was immediately welcomed in to the kitchen where Mrs. Aronovitch and I chatted like old friends while last minute prep was under way. The Aronovitch family is a very special mishpacha, to say the least. I was privileged to have the second seder by them for Pesach this year. Mrs. Aronovitch was so gracious to me and insisted that I spend the night on her couch rather than walking the 3 miles home. She even insisted on setting the couch with sheets and pillows for me, despite my insistence it was unnecessary. They are a very special family, and their children are involved in both kiruv and very high-level learning; everyone was made to feel comfortable at their table, including people who are not Orthodox, and the hachnasat orchim was amazing. Mrs. Aronovitch so selflessly looks after her guests, even at the expense of her own comfort, and Mr. Aronovitch did a wonderful job at saying over the peshat of the Haggadah. I find his combination of frumkeit, secular learning, and his concern and love for all peoples to be inspirational. They are also a highly learned family, and their library consists of thousands of history,

I had the best Shabbat dinner with the Lasker family. Yenty was very helpful with directions getting there, and they welcomed me right into their family. It was great to meet other traveling Jews from all over the world, and even though I was all the way in Brussels, it felt just like home! Highly recommend. Thank you again!
Amazing hospitality! Thank you so much for having us, it was a very important Shabat in our trip and we'll always remember it!
Thank you very much for the wonderful Shabbos! We enjoyed it immensely!

Wonderful host! It was a delightful experience to have Shabbat with the Lasker family. They make you feel very welcome and Rebbetzin Lasker is an excellent cook. Rabbi Lasker also has a great sense of humor. I may need to return to Brussels again in the near future and will be sure to inquire as to their availability if I do.

I had the honor and priveledge to experience first had the amazing hospitality and warmth of the Lasker family. Rabbi and Mrs. Lasker along with their children were the most generous and attentive hosts, and spending Shabbat in Brussels with them was an unforgatable experience. 

I'm so grateful to have had the pleasure of meeting them and spending a lovely Shabbat there. I can't wait to see them on their next visit to NY.

In the spiritual wilderness of Brussels, Rabbi & Mrs Lasker's home projects warmth and comfort and is open to every Jew who has to spend Shabbos in the city, on business and pleasure alike. It was not by chance that I ended up in their home on Shabbos Vayera, when the analogy with Avraham Avinu ushering guests into his tent couldn't have been more fitting!

Besides the sumptuous table and delicious cuisine (the taste of Mrs Lasker's cholunt still lingering in my mouth!), you get a spiritual intake that is even more satiating than the food -- divrei Torah, insights and, most amazingly, real-life stories of the kind that just could not have been made up (my favourite was about a dairy plant using pig gelatine!)

(continued from above)
... If you do end up at the Laskers' Shabbos table, you'll most certainly find yourself in the company of wandering Jews from far and near, as it was in my case, - three Israelis, one South American and a couple of locals, with Rabbi Lasker simultaneously supporting conversations in English, Hebrew, French and Yiddish. You'll find that many of the walls that separate Jews in other parts of the world are simply non-existent at the Laskers' table.

So for an experience like no other, in a place where the scarcity of Yiddishkeit makes the Laskers' hospitality stand out even more prominently, be sure to check yourself in with this wonderful family and you'll have a Shabbos to remember for a long time.

personal.about:
BLUF (Bottom Line Up Front):  56 years old. I have not made any babies as yet. I seek a companion first and foremost, not the mother of my children... 
What an interesting experience to have discovered this site! I am a small town living Jewish man who enjoys (craves) the company of  fellow Jews while understanding that most Jews are to be found in more urban or suburban areas. Sadly, I am at ease and most comfortable in G-d's country with dirt roads, a quiet breeze rustling through the branches and a slower pace.   I study Torah, daven daily, wear tzitzit, light the Shabbat candles weekly, and work a mean chainsaw.  And you?

datingProfile.About_Me:
56 Years old. Single. I have yet to make a baby or babies, and while I am open-minded, I am not seeking the mother of my children. First and foremost, I seek my lifetime companion. And likely she would be at an age where she is not looking to make any (more) babies...

I am being asked if I have a dating resume (A dating resume?!?). My goodness, has it come to that? I have read that a first date is like a job interview: Put your best foot forward, wear your Shabbat finest, etc.  How about I present to you the man that you will see every moment of every day. Direct, thoughtful, intuitive, engaged and engaging (I hope), attentive. A man. Masculine, a problemsolver, a deep thinker. A man who feels Hashem's presence always, and strives to nurture that relationship with Him. Our (yours and my) relationship will come next. If we both cherish our relationship as we cherish a baby that we may have made (some years ago), I am certain that the relationship will thrive. But mostly, understand that I am a country living man. I am compromising and considerate, but on this, I shan't budge. Small town, but not the city. *deep sigh* I lost most of you....
datingProfile.Looking_For:
You?   Ideally, you are content, serene, perhaps even sanguine. Thoughtful, introspective, self-aware, Jewish(!), want to bring the best out of your partner and encourage him to support you in the same fashion. We may study Torah together or separately, or both. You are health-conscious, mindful living, intentional living. You may be taller ,shorter, dark hair, light hair, gray hair, none of that matters. Your dress size and breast size are of no matter, either.

But first and foremost, you will enjoy small town/country living. I know this is a difficult  one....

The ideal relationship is a friendship, where both partners are actively on the lookout for ways to give to the other.

I married a brilliant and beautiful woman from China.  She converted to Judaism prior to our marriage.  G-d blessed us with two children and two grandchildren.  My wife lost a valiant battle with cancer.

I have devoted my career to institutional investment management. The field has been challenging and interesting.  I have made many friends.  I have been active with several Jewish charities.

I have resumed the study of classical piano following a 35-year quiet period.

I seek a woman who is deeply committed to Judaism, is highly intelligent and loves music.

personal.about:
I observe Shabbat and the major holidays, keep kosher, study, participate in synagogue life, am on the L.A. board of the AJC, and help organize the Shabbos Project.

That said, I tend to take a more scholarly view of scripture, and don’t necessarily agree with all of Halakha, but I am quite passionate about Judaism and proud to be Jewish.  I incorporate Jewish practice into my life to honor our ancient and amazing heritage and to be a living participant in Jewish life and community.  

You might call me “Reservadox”.  For example, I separate milk and meat (kosher of course), but I don’t believe two sets of dishes are required with modern non-porous dishware.  On the other hand, if my match wants two sets of dishes, we’ll have two sets of dishes!  I’ve learned what battles to pick :)

I'm ambitious and work hard, but not a workaholic.  I'm an understanding, honest, supportive and affectionate partner.

datingProfile.About_Me:
I'm thoughtful and generally a bit reserved, but at the same time friendly, fun and sociable.  I'm emotionally available and can express my feelings easily when I want. I'm perceptive and understanding, caring and supportive.  

I'm Ashkenazi, was raised in a secular home, but have come to value living a Jewish life and being an active participant in the Jewish community.  I do tend toward having more of an academic (scholarly) view towards Torah.  I don't have the same spiritual orientation as many who grew up in orthodox homes, but I take the position that observance is more important anyway. In that regard, I keep Kosher for the most part, keep Shabbat and the major holidays, attend synagogue on many Shabbats, study and am involved with the AJC and the Shabbos Project.  That said, I don't agree with all common interpretations of what is required to be an observant Jew.  But of course, I'm Jewish -- how agreeable do you expect me to be?

I have a wide range of interests, including Judaism (of course), a scholarly interest in the development of Christianity (and am sometimes involved in anti-missionary efforts), biblical archaeology, history, the natural sciences, current events, news and politics.

I'm in excellent health and active. Not a gym rat, but I do exercise regularly.  I love outdoor activities, such as playing tennis, hiking, camping and cycling (road and mountain)  I particularly love being near the ocean.
datingProfile.Looking_For:
For me, what's inside is far more important than the outside. However, I must feel very attracted to a woman because I'm a passionate man, and so I do look for what it's commonly considered to be attractive.  

That being said, the personal characteristics I find attractive include warmth, nurturing, affection & sensuality, intelligence (both IQ and EQ), understanding, wisdom, ethics and morals. I prefer someone calm and soft spoken.

I'm a warm, upbeat, and gregarious guy. I’m a hopeless optimist, and my mantra is that good things are right around the corner.  Religiously I'm somewhere in the middle of the yeshiva and modern worlds, without any difficulty relating to either.  If my personal leanings were slightly one way versus the other though, I lean more to the right in terms of practice and principle.  
My mother’s family runs eight generations deep in Israel, and my father’s family goes back six generations there as well, with both families hailing from the holy city of Tzfat.  I was born and raised in NY, so if you’re expecting an Israeli showing up at your door with hummus on his sleeves and collar, you’re going to be sorely disappointed.  I have a younger married sister who lives in Queens as well, but being that I’ve accumulated an immense amount of both useful and utterly useless knowledge over the years, she pretty much only calls me when she needs advice or a favor (usually it’s the latter).  Joking aside though, I’ve never been married, but hoping to change that even through this very not run-of-the-mill resume you’ve been reading in your current state of shock. personal.about: I am a happy and warm person. I love Shabbos and consider it holy and a gift from HaShem. datingProfile.About_Me: I am a Baal Teshuva and a Zionist and extremely passionate about Judaism. I regret that I didn't connect with my Jewish faith many years ago, but as with many of the Jews in the USA, I was totally assimilated. But B"H...G-d led me back home! I have one son who is a young Chabad Rabbi and has blessed me with 2 grandchildren with more on the way! I am a sponge for knowledge ... I read about some area of Judaism every day with hopes of making changes so that I can grow closer to HaShem and become the best Jew possible (hope to be considered an Ayshes Chayil someday!) I love to read books about famous Jewish sages such as the Baal Shem Tov, Rabbi Akiva, etc. I love reading numerous commentaries on the weekly parsha. I have read "Garden of Emuna" by Rabbi Arush a few times ... this book has taught me about how vital it is to have "complete" faith in HaShem no matter what life's circumstances are. Much more to tell but there isn't enough space here to write more.

personal.about: Hello...  I am a graduate of the physical therapy program at the University of Findlay and have served in this profession for over 20 years. I have two daughters and six grandchildren. I enjoy listening to shiurim for hours, gardening, hiking, cycling, living simple, reading and  research.  I am probably an information junkie (useful info for purposes of chessed) since I don't believe one should ever stop learning.  I am shomer shabbat, 100% kosher, not much of a meat eater (perhaps fish or chicken 1-2 days/week), I attend torah study weekly, daven daily.  I am very serious about living a life pleasing to HaShem and keeping mitzvot. I have read through tanakh from cover to cover probably 15 times and continue to do so. I would love to share my life with someone who is serious about Torah and wishes to share theirs with me if HKB would have it to be so.  Everyone is amazing in their own unique way.  Looking forward to meeting you!

datingProfile.About_Me:
I'm not one who talks about themselves, but I suppose I could add a few things about my personality. If the needle were in the middle and slightly right leaning on the introvert (R) extrovert (L) scale, I tend to lean more towards being introvert but can jump into action and take control when needed.  I enjoy interacting with people and hearing their stories and then later retreat into quiet contemplation.  I tend to be positive and one who looks for solutions. I don't like to kvetch and believe that all things ultimately come from HaShem. I am one who encourages, listens, empathizes.  I am aware of my own short comings, failures, and limitations and quickly seek to improve myself. I am also practical in that I like to set goals... steps to success. I realize that change takes time, for myself and for others, and that patience and understanding go a long way in any relationship.

I am about 85% vegetarian and would love to be able to grow my own food and share it. I have been blessed by HKB with good health and enjoy helping others to achieve this or their best selves they can be.  I am a caretaker at heart, generous, kind, intuitive, attentive to detail, and believe that the weightiest part of communication is often what is not said.
datingProfile.Looking_For:
I am looking to make acquaintances and have already met some wonderful individuals on this site. I am also hopeful to meet my soulmate (may it be soon in my days) here or out there somewhere. Shidduchim are in G-d's hands and I have complete emunah and bitachon in His timing.

The qualities that cause me to take notice and say, "I must turn aside and see this great sight..." include one who loves HaShem, passionate about Torah study and spiritual growth, one who is kind, patient, honest with his feelings, approachable and not argumentative, thoughtful, and loving.

At this stage in life, marriage for me is not a fairy-tale. It will most definitely mean two individuals coming together to blend half a lifetime of experiences. What it should not mean is looking to continue the past but rather anticipation of creating a new, unique, and exciting future.  I don't expect that we will have all the same likes, interests, or opinions, but should be able to delight in the appreciation of what makes the other happy.

From the very first time I stepped foot in Israel, I knew I had to make it my home. Six years later I was fortunate enough to make my dream a reality. Life here really is both a dream and at times a harsh reality. I have grown in ways I don’t think would be possible if I lived anywhere else in the world. 
I love to be creative. I write for a living and I really enjoy that it allows me to express my creative and analytical side at the same time. When I’m not playing with words, I’m playing with paints or sometimes colored pencils. Creating art both challenges and relaxes me. 
To me Judaism isn't just a religion; it is a way of life. I know I am both spiritual as well as grounded. I like to understand the deeper meanings behind Jewish concepts and rituals, but also understand that the mitzvot are integral for being a Torah-observant Jew. I really embrace my role as a Jewish woman as I strive to have a healthy balance of both softness as well as strength. 
Connecting with others is something that energizes me. I love meeting new people and spending time with close friends, whether that be going on adventures together, or cooking dinner and catching up. Baruch HaShem, I have been blessed with many special people in my life, including a family I am very close with.

I am extremely passionate about kiruv, and I would love to find someone who shares that passion, but it isn't a must. I’m also pretty outgoing, so I’m looking for someone who is quite social as well. I would love to have a large and lively Shabbat table.

Hey Gents, I wish you all lots of luck on here. Online dating is brutal and cold and largely heartless in my opinion. But I can't seem to find any of you at Home Depot or the lumber yard. We're not perfect people, and we're always falling and getting back up. But that's part of the beauty of life. I'm not close to where I dream to be but every day starts with. "Damn I'm Proud to be a Jew!"
I believe Shabbas is the gift of all gifts. I find nothing more satisfying and attractive then a hard day of honest work. Family life is paramount. I believe in being there for the ones you love. Helping out when you can and when it's inconvenient. But I also know the importance of taking care of ones own self. A not frequent enough indulgence of mine is a drive up, where the scenery blurs out the decades leaving just nature.  I'm always up for Sushi. I'm always down for a good horror/fantasy film. I'm insecure about too much. I'm cocky about my driving. I'll shut up and listen when people talk about the beauty of other people. There's usually dirt under my nails. I love red lip stick. Music is in every breath I breathe. My son is my top priority. Being responsible for and held accountable for a child (5 year old boy (Poo poo poo) going on 15) is the most scariest thing ever! My overwhelming love for him and my Emunah that G-d has a plan for him. And has my back 100% of the time. keeps me down to normal human rational every day life. I love big. I cry alone. I'm always working on my short temper. I'm gonna end this with.   If I or any woman for that matter doesn't respond to your messages on this site or any other. Well, You got 2 happy choices. 1: Don't waist your time and move on you'll find better. Or 2: don't give up Listen to your gut and push harder for what you want.

datingProfile.About_Me:
I am a widow with 9 year old triplets. What else is there to say? Honestly, a lot. I am also a daughter, sister, dog lover, penguin collector, bookworm, librarian and Olah Chadashah.

I am an avid reader and love discussion and debate on all different topics. I also love movies and television shows in a broad range of genres. I am a giver. My greatest joy comes from providing friends and family with a listening ear, a needed hug, advice and support. 

I work very hard to live by "Ivdu et Hashem b'simcha." I believe that you must constantly be growing in Torah U'Mitzvot in some way, however small, all the time. I know that life is too short to spend it on petty fights, Sinat Chinam, and regrets. I believe in working to live your dreams and living your best life. We made Aliyah in 2011 in a desire to live our dreams. I am currently living in the wonderful Yishuv of Neve Daniel, where my brother's family and parents live.
datingProfile.Looking_For:
I don't like to put absolutes on the type of person that I am looking for, because I believe that you can't make a list of what you want. People aren't lists and check-boxes, they are multi-faceted. 

My ideal relationship is a true partnership, sharing responsibilities in the relationship and for the relationship. It is based on mutual respect, love, shared goals and dreams. Relationships should bring out the best in both members.

Ultimately, I am looking for a partner who will love me for who I am, inspire me, and help me grow. Someone who is kind, sensitive, and generous in all areas. He should see the beauty of Yiddishkeit and living a Torah life. Someone who wants a life filled with passion, laughter, excitement, dedication, and a lot of quiet nights at home too. He should look forward to loving my children, helping me raise them, and growing our family.

datingProfile.About_Me:
I am a published author, and have a Ph.D. in Jewish Studies, with an emphasis in Jewish Spirituality (Hasidism, Kabbalah) and Jewish philosophy. My books and articles discuss Jewish and universal spirituality, psychology, caring/loving personal relationships, and compassionate transformation of society. The basic purpose of my writing, teaching, and personal life is to promote deep connection to one's own soul or core integrity, as well as loving connection to other individuals, G-d, and the world of nature. My outlook is similar to Jewish philosophers such as, Martin Buber, Abraham Joshua Heschel, Arthur Waskow, and Abraham Isaac Kook, as well as Jewish psychologists such as Erich Fromm, Alfred Adler, and others.

My life is like a treasure hunt, seeking to reveal or discover/uncover hidden sparks of holiness, beauty, goodness, or wonder-full "magic" in my encounters with other people, as well as in my daily activities and experiences. I like to mentor and dialogue with other people.
datingProfile.Looking_For:
I seek a woman whose basic personal qualities and values are similar to mine, especially in terms of being sincere/honest/trustworthy, open-minded, peaceful/easygoing, affectionate, caring/loving/warmhearted, deeply spiritual, soulful/wise/inspirational.

I have learned that developing good relationships requires much hard work, mutually respectful constructive sincere empathic communication, patience, resilience, flexibility, and nonjudgmental acceptance of the natural wholeness of the other person. I find that investing my whole being in developing that kind of relationship with the right kind of person is well worth the effort.

You are probably "my type" if you are eager to give your whole being, your whole heart and soul, to a relationship, and are eager to know and be known truly and deeply. If you are a sensitive soul, who is open to letting life experience and love touch you deeply, and who is much more interested in inner beauty than outer attractiveness, let's connect!

I always leave the Klatzko home hoping to return as soon as possible for another Shabbos with them. It is truly a wonderful environment to spend Shabbos!

And as sad as it was to see shabbos go, this weeks havdalah was probably my favorite one yet! With the music being more lively than ever and more songs added and to end the havdalah in the Sukkah on Hoshana Raba was incredible! Anyone who hasn’t gone yet please make it your will to do so!

Tizku Lmitzvot

Best place in the world.  So loving, caring kind and "homey" environment. I think hashem loves what you guys do. Definitly changed my life.

You changed my life and outlook on Shabbat and I can’t thank you enough for that. I cannot wait to come back again and again (BZH!) to spend Shabbat with such holy and special people. May Hashem give you many more years to come to inspire and continue people time and time again as well as wealth,happiness,simchot and so much more. I can go on and on again but I just wanted to thank you again for everything. Was truly an amazing Shabbat. We should only hear good things and I’ll see you in Jerusalem... Amen!

"???? ???? ???? ??????"

personal.about:
In order to reserve and be accepted at the Klatzko home, you must have a picture of yourself on your profile.
Please be aware, if you have not requested through the "Host Me" button on the site, and received confirmation, we will not have a bed for you. 
No gift is expected. 
However, if you do wish to bring something, our favorites our cheesecake (we serve it by the kiddush Shabbat morning) or Baron Herzog late harvest riesling wine.

Please be careful to obey street signs on our block. They do ticket and tow.
If there is no more parking on our block, please go 2 doors up Margetts and park in the public school there. It is a few minutes walk from our home.
If you would like to bring a friend or friends, please be aware that each must reserve on Shabbat.com separately. 
We usually make a late Shabbat. If you are coming from Brooklyn or the Manhattan and driving, please give yourself plenty of time to make your way through Friday traffic.
You can also take the Monsey Trails bus (http://monseytrails.com/)
You can also go to the website and see who else is coming from your area and message them.
Sleeping is "first come first serve" so if you wish to stay out our home and not at a neighbors house, please come early. 
We will try our best to accommodate your seeping requests. However, due to the usual volume of people, we may not be able to. 
Our address is: 4 Wannamaker Court, Monsey NY 10952
